text.p: Jayhawk Acceptance Corp said Friday it has filed with a bankruptcy court a proposed plan of reorganization which has been agreed to by its primary lender.

Under the plan, Jayhawk said it will continue its business operations and pay its creditors in full. The primary lender will be repaid in monthly installments with the view to having the full amount paid by September 1998, according to a company spokeswoman.
Jayhawk said it has filed its 10-K annual report with regulators showing 1996 revenues of $53.6 million and a net loss of $49.7 million.
It said the net loss reflects adjustments resulting from measures taken in connecion with its Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection proceeding and a lower number of contracts for purchase consideration.
In addition, the loss also reflects the company's recognition that it will not be doing the same level of business with dealers in the near future as it was doing before the Chapter 11 filing.
Jayhawk said that as a result of a reevaluation, it increased its previously-announced fourth quarter special charge to $66.5 million, increasing its allowance for credit losses.

The company said it expects that because of the Chapter 11 proceeding and the 1996 net loss, its independent auditors' report will express doubts about the company;s ability to continue as a going concern.
Jayhawk is a specialized financial services company based in Dallas, Texas.
